models.title: Building-block exchange-rate expectation
models.summary: Expected currency move equals the sum of short-rate, term, credit, equity and liquidity premium differentials.

relationship.original_equation: E(%ΔSd/f) = (rd − rf) + (Termd − Termf) + (Creditd − Creditf) + (Equityd − Equityf) + (Liquidd − Liquidf)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Forecasting Exchange Rates, printed p. 102 (PDF p. 112), Equation 9
relationship.translation_notes: PDF prints percentages; record uses decimal form per session convention (1.25% as 0.0125). Each parenthesized differential is domestic minus foreign for one portfolio segment (money market through private assets). UIP is the special case where only the first term matters. Dimensional check: dimensionless + dimensionless terms = dimensionless expected change.

assumptions: Perfect capital mobility equalizes risk-adjusted expected returns across the two currency portfolios at the forecast horizon.
Each premium differential is measured over the same horizon and comparable segments.
limitations: Long-run phase relationship (Phase 3 of the overshooting mechanism); short-run flows and overshooting can move the spot rate the opposite way.
Carry-trade evidence shows UIP (the first-term-only special case) predicts poorly; the premium terms carry the explanatory load.

models.title: After-tax expected return scaling
models.summary: Expected after-tax return equals pre-tax return scaled by one minus the expected tax rate.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM5 After-Tax Portfolio Optimization, printed p. 325 (PDF p. 335), Equation 1
relationship.translation_notes: PDF prints percentages; record uses decimal form per session convention (3% as 0.03). Single blended expected tax rate; the dividend/cap-gain split (PDF Eq2) is deferred for lack of independent corroboration. Dimensional check: dimensionless × dimensionless = dimensionless return.

variables.definition: Expected pre-tax (gross) return, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset class and forecast horizon as rat

variables.definition: Expected tax rate applied to the return, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset class and forecast horizon as rat

variables.definition: Expected after-tax return, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset class and forecast horizon as inputs

assumptions: Single blended expected rate captures the tax drag (interest-like treatment); mixed dividend/cap-gain streams need the PDF's split form.
limitations: Approximation for modeling: ignores holding-period effects on capital-gains realization and embedded gains (per source footnotes).
Losses are muted symmetrically by the same factor (capital-loss benefit assumed realizable).

models.title: After-tax standard deviation scaling
models.summary: Expected after-tax volatility equals pre-tax volatility scaled by one minus the expected tax rate.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM5 After-Tax Portfolio Optimization, printed p. 326 (PDF p. 336), Equation 3
relationship.translation_notes: σat/σpt ASCII aliases for the PDF's subscripted sigmas. Same (1 − t) factor as the return scaling (shared t meaning). Correlations are unaffected (after-tax co-movements equal pre-tax). Dimensional check: dimensionless × dimensionless = dimensionless dispersion.

variables.definition: Expected pre-tax standard deviation, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset class and forecast horizon as sig_at

variables.definition: Expected tax rate, in decimal form (same meaning as after-tax return record)
variables.context: same asset class and forecast horizon as sig_at

variables.definition: Expected after-tax standard deviation, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset class and forecast horizon as inputs

assumptions: Tax truncates both tails proportionally (lower highs, higher lows), so dispersion scales linearly with the same factor as the mean.
limitations: Correlations assumed unchanged; joint tail behavior under asymmetric tax codes may deviate.
Same modeling approximation as the return scaling (ignores realization timing).

models.title: After-tax rebalancing range gross-up
models.summary: The taxable investor's rebalancing range equals the pre-tax range divided by one minus the tax rate.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM5 Taxes and Portfolio Rebalancing, printed p. 329 (PDF p. 339), Equation 4; example 0.10/(1 − 0.25) = 13.3%
relationship.translation_notes: Wider after-tax range follows from muted after-tax volatility: larger pre-tax moves are needed to match the risk change of the tax-exempt range. Decimal form (10% as 0.10). Dimensional check: dimensionless / dimensionless = dimensionless range.

variables.definition: Pre-tax (tax-exempt-investor) rebalancing range deviation, in decimal form
variables.context: same target allocation and risk constraint as Rat

variables.definition: Expected tax rate on the asset's returns, in decimal form (same meaning as after-tax records)
variables.context: same asset and risk constraint as Rat

variables.definition: After-tax (taxable-investor) rebalancing range deviation for the same risk constraint, in decimal form
variables.context: same target allocation and risk constraint as Rpt

assumptions: Ranges are compared from the same gross-return perspective for an equivalent risk constraint.
Correlations unchanged after tax, so the widening comes only through the volatility scaling.
limitations: Wider ranges reduce trading and taxable gains but let the allocation drift further; the trade-off depends on owner circumstances (per source).
Mean-reversion beliefs can argue for tighter bands, opposing the tax-widening (per curriculum context).

models.title: After-tax value of tax-deferred assets
models.summary: After-tax value of tax-deferred assets equals pre-tax market value scaled by one minus the distribution tax rate.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM5 Asset location, printed p. 330 (PDF p. 340), Equation 5
relationship.translation_notes: Partnership view: the investor owns (1 − ti) of the account, the government owns ti. Tax-deferred assets grow at pre-tax rates (inputs unadjusted); only the value is haircut. ti is the expected income tax rate at distribution, distinct from the return-drag t. Dimensional check: currency × dimensionless = currency value.

variables.definition: Pre-tax market value of assets in the tax-deferred account, in currency units
variables.context: same account and distribution event as vat

variables.definition: Expected income tax rate upon distribution, in decimal form
variables.context: same account and distribution event as vat

variables.definition: After-tax value of the tax-deferred assets, in currency units
variables.context: same account and distribution event as inputs

assumptions: Distribution is taxable as modeled (no basis recovery, no penalty, no bequest step-up in this approximation).
Tax-deferred assets use pre-tax return and risk inputs in the optimization; the value haircut carries the tax adjustment.
limitations: As-if-sold-today approximation: ignores discounting the liability to a future sale date (alternatives in Horan/Al Zaman, Turvey et al. per source).
Tax-exempt accounts need no adjustment; this equation is for tax-deferred accounts only.
